title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: A is a commutative Dedekind ring with fraction field K. A category C is A-preadditive: its Hom sets are A-modules and composition is A-bilinear. As the margin says, this is the same as a preadditive category together with a ring map A -> End(id_C).

Definition. C is a 'Deuring category relative to A' if condition (D) holds: there is an object X such that
(a) O = End(X) is a maximal A-order in E = End(X) (x)_A K, and E is an Azumaya (central simple) K-algebra;
(b) for every right O-module P that is 'projective of rank 1' the object P (x)_O X exists in C. The marginal gloss makes clear that 'rank 1' means locally on Spec A isomorphic to O, i.e. an invertible or locally principal right O-ideal class, not rank 1 over A;
(c) the functor P |-> P (x)_O X is an equivalence from the category of such right O-modules to C.
In modern terms this is the 'Serre tensor construction' carried out in an abstract linear category.

Independence of X. Grothendieck shows that if (D) holds for one object it holds for every object. By (c) one may take C = Proj_1(O) and an arbitrary object P. Then:
- O' = End_O(P), the left order of the ideal P, is again a maximal order in the same algebra E.
- If Q is a locally-free rank-1 right O'-module, then Q (x)_{O'} P is a locally-free rank-1 right O-module, since locally everything is O.
- Q |-> Q (x)_{O'} P is an equivalence (Morita theory). The next page gives the quasi-inverse P' |-> Hom_C(P,P').

Next page. He classifies such categories by Morita classes of A-orders, using bimodules invertible on both sides. Maximal orders in the same K-algebra are all equivalent through the connecting ideal O.O'. He also notes that Morita-equivalence preserves maximality.

Purpose. This axiomatizes the Deuring correspondence: supersingular elliptic curves over F_p-bar with A = Z form exactly such a category for a maximal order in B_{p,infinity}. The same holds for abelian varieties with CM by a maximal order (End = O_K, giving Pic). In a 1965 manuscript on the Galois theory of motives, it presumably serves as a model for the integral structure of a simple isogeny class (a 'motive with integral coefficients') whose endomorphism algebra is a division or central simple algebra.
errors: Next page: the connecting ideal sigma.sigma' should lie in the algebra E (= sigma (x) K), not 'in K'.

The margin's suggestion that a) is dispensable given b) and c) is false. For any order O (maximal or not), the category of locally-free rank-1 right O-modules satisfies b) and c) with X = O. So a) is logically independent of b) and c), as the second marginal note itself says.

In (a), 'Azumaya over K' should be read as central simple with centre exactly K. If End(X) (x) K has a larger centre L, one must take A to be the integral closure, or the definition fails. This is a gap in generality, not in logic.

The verification of a) for an arbitrary object, i.e. that the left order of a locally principal ideal of a maximal order is maximal, is only asserted ('résulte du fait'). The fact is classical and correct.

ideas.what: Abstract notion of a 'Deuring category': an A-linear category equivalent, via X |-> P (x)_O X, to invertible right modules over a maximal order in a central simple K-algebra.
ideas.modern_name: Categorical Deuring correspondence / category of invertible modules over a maximal order
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring (1941) for the supersingular case. The categorical formulation is usually credited to Waterhouse (1969), Kohel (1996) and Voight's 'Quaternion Algebras' (ch. 42).

ideas.what: Tensor construction P (x)_O X of an object X of a linear category by a projective module over its endomorphism ring.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (c. 1967, Cassels–Fröhlich), Giraud; modern write-ups by Conrad and others.

ideas.what: Independence of the base object: every invertible module over a maximal order has a maximal left order, and tensoring is an equivalence.
ideas.modern_name: Morita theory for maximal orders; Brandt groupoid / connecting ideals

ideas.what: Classification of such categories by Morita classes of orders. Maximal orders of the same algebra are all equivalent through O.O'.
ideas.modern_name: Morita equivalence of maximal orders (locally conjugate orders form one genus)

missed.claim: Grothendieck abstracts Deuring's supersingular correspondence into an axiomatic notion of a 'Deuring category' over any Dedekind ring and any central simple algebra. He places it inside his 1965 'Galois theory of motives'. This implicitly unifies, as integral-coefficient versions of simple motives with maximal-order endomorphisms, two later results: the supersingular Deuring correspondence and the equivalences for CM abelian varieties with End = O_K (Waterhouse 1969, Deligne 1969). It does so years before the usual categorical formulations.
missed.quote: Une catégorie A-préadditive C est dite "catégorie de Deuring (relative à A)" si ... Le foncteur P ↦ P⊗_O X est une équivalence de catégories
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The categorical Deuring correspondence is now central to isogeny-based cryptography and to the arithmetic of supersingular loci. An early abstract framing, tied to integral motives, documents Grothendieck's thinking about integral structures on motives with endomorphisms. In the published record this notion is not attributed to him.

missed.claim: The definition is set up, but the intended application to motives (which categories of motives or abelian varieties are Deuring categories, e.g. isogeny classes over finite fields) is not visible on this page.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a possible early seed of questions about integral models of motives in an isogeny class with maximal-order endomorphisms (cf. Waterhouse, Jordan–Keeton–Poonen–Rains–Shepherd-Barron–Tate on abelian varieties isogenous to a power of an elliptic curve). Its significance depends on the surrounding pages.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is classical: maximal orders, Morita theory and the Deuring correspondence. What is notable is the abstract, named axiomatization 'catégorie de Deuring' in 1965 inside the motives notes, using the Serre tensor construction categorically. This anticipates later categorical formulations but proves nothing new.
transcription_corrections: Marginal note on the first line should read roughly: '(i.e. les Hom sont des A-modules, et l'accouplement des Hom bilinéaire) ⟺ C est préadditive, donnée d'un hom. d'anneaux A → End(id_C)'.
In b) the crossed-out text after 'P⊗_O' is 'X' plus a struck word; the intended reading is 'P ⊗_O X existe comme objet de C'.
The insertion beside b) reads roughly '(i.e. loc. sur Spec A isomorphe à O^1 ...)', i.e. locally isomorphic to O; the marks after it are uncertain.
In the verification of a): 'le commutant O' de O dans P est un ordre maximal d'une algèbre d'Azumaya (en fait, de E lui-même)'.

The diagonal left-margin NB is uncertain. A plausible reading is 'NB La condition a) est indispensable, b) et c) sont raisonnablement indépendantes'; the lower margin note reads 'a) est ... indépendante de b) et c)'.
Next page: 'σ.σ' ... ⊂ K' should be read as a subset of E (likely a slip by the author or the transcriber).
